key_insight: Fourier-circuit configuration affects both LiDAR classification accuracy and noise sensitivity, with IQFT-After leading on ideal KITTI simulations but degrading more under quantum noise.
engineering_relevance: Hardware-aware circuit selection matters: removing final QFT SWAP gates reduces complexity while preserving Pauli-Z features up to a fixed permutation absorbable by the classifier.
method: Combine PointNet feature extraction, amplitude encoding, and a variational quantum circuit.
Compare No-QFT, Full-QFT-After, QFT-no-swap, IQFT-After, and Trainable-QFT.
Evaluate classification, class-level behavior, circuit complexity, and simulated noise robustness.
evidence_signal: Evaluation on KITTI, nuScenes, and PandaSet across three seeds found ideal KITTI weighted F1 of 0.857 ± 0.033 for IQFT-After versus 0.838 ± 0.023 for No-QFT; IBM FakeManilaV2 noise changed the circuit ranking.
watch_item: Ideal-simulation gains do not establish hardware advantage; noise robustness and dataset-dependent minority-class performance require careful validation.
paper_title: QFT-Based Hybrid PointNet-Quantum Neural Networks for LiDAR Point-Cloud Classification
